headline: Astra Edits Model Weights by Hand
lede: Astra experiments with a strange new interface to neural networks: natural-language instructions aimed directly at their weights. The early results are narrow but notable, improving Qwen3.5-0.8B after changing just 0.016 percent of its parameters.

headline: NVIDIA Opens an Ontology for Enterprise Data
lede: Auto Ontology builds a semantic layer from database metadata, then exposes it through APIs, a CLI, and an MCP server. It promises cleaner agent-assisted analytics; credentials stored in plaintext by default suggest a less-clean deployment story.

headline: Toit Reaches Version 2 After Four Years
lede: Toit 2.0 ships after more than 2,000 commits and 200-plus releases. The embedded language brings a unified toolchain, a rewritten package manager, broader hardware support, and a final planned breaking change.

headline: This Tool Burns Pictures Into Optical Discs
lede: DiscImageStudio converts images into the physical patterns that CD, DVD, and Blu-ray burners can record. Calibration, dithering, simulation, and experimental direct burning turn obsolete media into a low-resolution canvas.

headline: Katamari Rolls Through the Metropolitan Museum
lede: KatamariMet turns the Met’s CC0 collection into a timed browser game: roll through a gallery, collect artifacts, and grow large enough to absorb the Temple of Dendur. Cultural heritage becomes wonderfully, cheerfully physical.

headline: Hacker News Gets the Newspaper Treatment
lede: Hacker Times reframes the HN front page as an hourly newspaper, with rewritten headlines, summaries, and a more deliberate reading rhythm. It is a contemporary interface built from an old editorial instinct: make the information legible.

headline: Europe Builds a Long-Lived RISC-V Stack
lede: ERICI proposes an open reference platform for industrial computers built around the RVA23 RISC-V profile. Firmware, hypervisors, real-time software, and Linux are designed to coexist on hardware expected to remain supportable for 10 to 15 years.

headline: Subvocal Turns Silent Mouthing Into Text
lede: Subvocal’s smart glasses use radio-frequency sensing to detect silent articulation and convert it into text at speaking speed. The prototype points toward quieter computer input, while accuracy, privacy, comfort, and the planned 2027 shipment remain open questions.

headline: Depth Becomes the Photograph
lede: Vathography treats an estimated depth map as the finished artwork rather than a temporary editing step. With ordinary photographs and open tools, artists can remap inferred volume into tone, color, and focus.

headline: When Efficient Algorithms Lose the Plot
lede: Asymptotic complexity gives computer science a durable vocabulary, but its labels can conceal enormous crossover points and practical irrelevance. A critique of exponential-time theory asks a more grounded question: which algorithms actually work at the sizes we face?
pullquote: A mathematically efficient algorithm can still be practically useless.
